question: Does the factor-50 theorem for H-minor-free graphs with pw(H) at most two certify dominance over the original K2,t-minor-free factor-50 result, including its round complexity?

conclusion.summary: The thesis explicitly reuses the same Algorithm 5. With H=K2,t, the original class control function, local-cut radii and component-exploration schedule give literally the original algorithm, whose O(t) analysis remains valid. A family implementing this original schedule on the mapped H=K2,t branch and the generic Chapter VIII schedule elsewhere covers the original result with strictness in the parameterized family of excluded-minor settings. No generic Chapter VIII diameter-threshold comparison is needed outside the mapped subfamily because the original theorem supplies no guarantee there. This does not assert faster rounds, a strict runtime improvement, or that every fixed H of pathwidth at most two defines a superclass of every K2,t-minor-free class.
conclusion.recommendedTreatment: An explicit same-algorithm/configuration certificate justifies marking the original theorem covered by the broader theorem, strictly in parameterized graph-family scope, while retaining its original citation as provenance. The certificate must preserve O(t) on H=K2,t and retain generic f(H) elsewhere. Mere graph inclusion plus the strings f(H),f(t) would not justify this comparison; the source-backed mapped identical-runtime certificate supplies the missing premise.
conclusion.runtimeComparisonOnMappedSubfamily: Identical implementation and O(t) guarantee under H=K2,t, using the original control function, local-cut radii, and residual exploration schedule.

findings.claim: K2,t has pathwidth two for every t>=2. Choosing H=K2,t specializes Theorem VIII.1.1 exactly to K2,t-minor-free input graphs. This concerns the excluded graph, not the pathwidth of the input graph.

findings.claim: Chapter VIII derives a residual-diameter threshold through the universal ladder L_k, with k=|V(H)|, a recursive almost-ladder bound, and a final additive four. No statement compares that generic threshold at H=K2,t with the earlier Ding-based linear threshold. The much larger proof expression is an upper bound and does not show that the actual same algorithm runs more slowly on K2,t inputs.

findings.claim: A family-wide implementation can use the original Algorithm 5 schedule for H=K2,t and the generic Chapter VIII schedule for other H. Since the mapped branch has the same approximation guarantee, problem/model/weights and O(t) schedule as the original, the broader parameterized theorem covers the old result. Strictness lies in the range of excluded-minor families, not in faster runtime on K2,t. A comparison of the generic ladder threshold with the old Ding threshold is neither claimed nor required on settings outside the old theorem’s domain.

certificateConditions: The problem is unweighted minimum dominating set with the integral benchmark, in deterministic LOCAL.
Instantiate the excluded graph H as K2,t, for fixed integer t>=2.
Use the same Algorithm 5, including the same true-twin reduction and residual domination implementation.
Use the K2,t class control function and local-cut radii from the original construction; the thesis supplies F_t(r)=(5r+18)t.
Use the original Chapter IV runtime analysis to retain O(t) on this specialization; do not infer a comparison of arbitrary unspecified f(H) and f(t) functions.
Keep any parameter restriction attached to the separate SOTA claim, such as the existing t>=49 review domain. Neither Theorem IV.3.1 nor VIII.1.1 itself requires t>=49.
limitations: The live thesis URL was not accessible through web extraction in this turn. Its already-downloaded primary-source PDF and pdftotext output were inspected locally at the cited PDF pages.
No numerical coefficients for Ding's linear function g(t) were audited, and no exact optimal round count is asserted.

The generic H-dependent runtime is not shown to improve the original parameter tradeoff. Same-algorithm identity under the stated configuration is stronger than mere class inclusion, but must be recorded as an explicit certificate rather than guessed from symbolic runtime labels.

vertexCoverRuntimeFollowup.explanation: The source explicitly extends both Theorems 4.1 and 4.3 to minimum vertex cover. It says it suffices to select all m2(C_t)-local 2-cuts instead of only the interesting vertices, using the same radius, together with the analogous simpler counting argument. The thesis repeats the extension immediately after the preceding page’s linear-in-t runtime analysis. This modification adds no larger inspection radius or iterative communication phase; the local-cut and bounded-residual-component approach therefore retains the O(t) asymptotic upper bound. The source does not separately print the string O(t) for vertex cover, so this is a bound derived from its stated extension and linear-radius analysis.
notClaimed: The exact integer expression 219t+g(t)+18 is not separately certified for the vertex-cover implementation.
No extension of the Chapter VIII pathwidth-two theorem to vertex cover is inferred by this runtime check.
No faster rounds or optimality of O(t) is claimed.
